page: Microsoft Azure D8as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

For local storage, the instance includes a 66 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2706.97 in stress-ng tests, which places it in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests, including read and write operations, consistently fall within the average range. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is relatively weak, registering in the bottom 25% at 35.43 GB/sec. Other workloads, such as Redis SET operations, static web serving, and small-model LLM inference, deliver average tier results.

From a resource density perspective, the D8as_v4 offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for general-purpose workloads. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC processing, moderate memory capacity, and local SSD storage makes it a viable option for applications requiring steady single-core performance without extreme multi-threaded demands. This virtual machine is well-suited for web serving, database operations, software compilation, and general application hosting.
